options.how: An AI storyteller (Cassandra, Phoebe, Randy) deals raids, storms and visitors into your colony; the story is what the colonists live through.
Writers script every beat of Nathan Drake's last adventure; cinematic cutscenes and set pieces play the same for every player.

sources.note: RimWorld: story generator driven by an AI storyteller
Uncharted 4: cinematic storytelling and a personal story for Nathan Drake

options.how: Characters with traits, genetics and schemes drive thousands of dynamic events; your dynasty's saga comes from simulation, not a script.
A written magical realist story in five acts; you choose how characters speak and feel, but the scenes and arc are authored.

sources.note: Crusader Kings III: dynasties, character traits and thousands of dynamic events
Kentucky Route Zero: a magical realist adventure in five acts

options.how: No main plot and no chosen one; capture, slavery or a rise to power happen through unscripted systems in a sandbox world.
A scripted father and son journey of Kratos and Atreus, told through cinema-quality scenes and in-play conversation.

sources.note: Kenshi: sandbox rather than a linear story, you are not the chosen one, no scripted events
God of War: Kratos and Atreus story with cinema-quality presentation

options.how: World generation simulates the rise and fall of civilizations and figures; stories come from what the simulation does to your dwarves.
Campaign chapters frame procedurally generated heroes and story events; heroes age, fall in love, feud and transform differently each run.
A scripted pilgrimage with Tidus and Yuna to defeat Sin; writers fix every plot beat and cutscene, and play happens between them.

sources.note: Dwarf Fortress: generated rise and fall of civilizations, personalities and cultures
Wildermyth: procedural generation gives new heroes and story events; heroes age and transform
Final Fantasy X: Tidus journeys with Yuna to save Spira from Sin

options.how: Quest choices have delayed consequences that surface hours later and combine into different epilogues and multiple endings.
One fixed story of Joel and Ellie; the player controls how encounters play out, never what happens in the plot.

sources.note: The Witcher 3: a story full of choices and consequences
The Last of Us: authored emotional storytelling

options.how: A charted branching narrative: decisions decide the fate of three leads, any of them can die and the story continues, toward dozens of endings.
A fixed noir revenge story told in chapters and comic panels; you choose how to shoot through each level, never the plot.

sources.note: Detroit: Become Human: branching narrative, characters can die, dozens of endings
Max Payne: cinematic action-shooter with a set story of a framed cop

options.how: Choices and failed actions can kill any of four leads; the hunt for the Origami Killer continues without them and the outcome shifts.
Episodes play in a set order with scripted twists and cliffhangers; combat and exploration happen between fixed story beats.

sources.note: Heavy Rain: every choice can have game-changing consequences
Alan Wake: TV-series structure with cliffhangers and plot twists

options.how: Side with NCR, Caesar's Legion, Mr. House or yourself; faction choices decide who holds the Mojave and which ending slides you get.
Tidus and Yuna's journey across Spira follows one scripted route; side content never changes the plot's events.

sources.note: Fallout: New Vegas: choose sides among warring factions to determine the outcome
Final Fantasy X: Tidus and Yuna's quest to save Spira from Sin

options.how: Pick your own route around a globe of 170 cities through thousands of text choices; every journey tells a different story.
A nearly textless journey through grief that unfolds the same way for everyone; abilities open new areas, not new story paths.

sources.note: 80 Days: choose your own route, 170 cities, thousands of choices
GRIS: almost textless journey through sorrow

options.how: Conversation choices reshape the Nameless One: his alignment, class and abilities change with what you say and do in Sigil.
A boy moves through one unbroken path into a dark project; there are no choices, only the puzzles between you and the next scene.

sources.note: Planescape: Torment: the Nameless One changes class, alignment and abilities based on choices
Inside: a boy drawn into the center of a dark project

options.how: Backstory hides in item and equipment descriptions, ruined architecture and sparse NPC lines; players piece the lore together.
Voiced cinematic conversations with a dialogue wheel; Paragon and Renegade choices carry the plot and relationships.

sources.note: Dark Souls: lore assembled from NPC dialogue hints and equipment descriptions
Mass Effect: cinematic saga with interactive storytelling and choices

options.how: No cutscenes or combat: you learn a family's story by picking up objects, notes and letters left around an empty house.
A film-like thriller of directed scenes, camera cuts and contextual prompts; the story is performed rather than found.

sources.note: Gone Home: discover the story by examining objects, notes and letters
Heavy Rain: psychological thriller with dramatic consequences

options.how: You collect pages of an in-game instruction manual whose illustrations, maps and hints reveal the world's secrets and history.
Performance-captured cutscenes and in-play banter carry the story; set pieces are staged like blockbuster film scenes.

sources.note: Tunic: collect missing manual pages with hints and illustrations
Uncharted 4: cinematic storytelling and blockbuster set pieces

options.how: No cutscene exposition: the dark project the boy uncovers is told through the rooms, machines and crowds you pass.
Episodic, voiced scenes with timed dialogue choices; the story of Lee and Clementine is carried by conversation and cutscenes.

sources.note: Inside: unsettling atmosphere and setting tell the story
The Walking Dead: episodic story of Clementine with character performances

options.how: No words: ruins, murals and wordless visions reveal an ancient civilization's history as you cross the desert toward a mountain.
A seamless, cut-free camera follows Kratos and Atreus; story is told through scripted scenes and conversation during play.

sources.note: Journey: explore an ancient, mysterious world to discover its secrets
God of War: seamless theatrical vision, cinema quality experience

options.how: You play Geralt of Rivia, a monster slayer with a fixed past, voice and relationships; choices steer him but he stays Geralt.
Create the Dragonborn's race, look and build; the hero is silent and unnamed in the story, so players project their own role.

sources.note: The Witcher 3: become monster slayer for hire Geralt of Rivia
Skyrim: open-ended RPG

options.how: You are Senua, a Celtic warrior with psychosis; her history, grief and psychosis are written, and the game is built around her mind.
Build your own hero from six races and eleven classes; the story reacts to your choices and reputation, not to a set personality.
Customize Shepard's look, gender and skills, but Shepard is a voiced, named Alliance officer with a fixed role in the story.

sources.note: Hellblade: a broken Celtic warrior, made with people who experience psychosis
Pillars of Eternity: six races, eleven classes, choices shape your destiny
Mass Effect: create and customize your own character

options.how: You play Max Caulfield, a photography student with her own voice, friendships and inner monologue; choices bend her story, not her identity.
Custom design as many characters as you like; none is special, and who they become is decided only by what happens to them.

sources.note: Life is Strange: Max Caulfield, a photography senior who can rewind time
Kenshi: custom design characters, you are not the chosen one

options.how: Max is a written character, an undercover cop whose family was murdered; his narration frames every level.
Create any kind of character from race, class and birthsign, then set off on your own; the hero's personality is left to the player.

sources.note: Max Payne: fugitive undercover cop uncovering the truth about his slain family
Morrowind: create and play any kind of character imaginable

options.how: You are Alan Wake, a best-selling writer hunting for his missing wife; his manuscript pages and narration drive the plot.
Create your own identity with race, class and background (or pick an Origin hero instead); companions react to the choices you make.

sources.note: Alan Wake: best-selling writer whose wife disappears
Baldur's Gate 3: create your own identity or play an Origin hero

options.how: 24 skills speak as inner voices that interject in conversation and gate dialogue checks; most problems are solved by talking.
Pick what Henry says to Delilah over a handheld radio, or stay silent; choices shape the relationship but there are no stat checks.
Peter Parker's story is told in voiced scenes and in-swing banter; you never pick lines, all dialogue plays as written.

sources.note: Disco Elysium: 24 skills and a revolutionary dialogue system
Firewatch: Delilah reachable over a handheld radio, choices shape the relationship
Marvel's Spider-Man: original story of Peter Parker

options.how: Dialogue options check fixed Speech, Barter and other skill scores; failed checks still show in red, so builds open or close solutions.
Characters talk constantly in cutscenes and while climbing, but you never choose a line; dialogue is fully scripted.

sources.note: Fallout: New Vegas: score-based skill checks in dialogue
Fallout: New Vegas: every skill given uses, including in dialogue
Uncharted 4: cinematic single-player story

options.how: Persuasion, Deception, Intimidation and knowledge checks roll a d20 plus modifiers against a DC, with bonuses you can add before rolling.
Speech bubbles pop up while you walk; pick one, interrupt or stay silent, and relationships shift, with no skill checks.
Sam's voiced journal entries play as you find objects; there are no conversations to steer and no lines to choose.

sources.note: Baldur's Gate 3: d20 skill checks in dialogue with bonuses
Oxenfree: conversation system that changes the story and relationships
Gone Home: story discovered by examining objects and notes

options.how: Skill checks such as Lore resolve scripted interactions, and faction and personality reputations change how characters respond to you.
Senua's psychosis is voiced as whispers that comment and argue in her ears; the player never picks a line of dialogue.

sources.note: Pillars of Eternity: official manual, Lore skill checks and the disposition system (faction and personality reputation)
Senua's Saga: Hellblade II: experience the world through Senua's eyes and ears as a warrior with psychosis

options.how: Lethal play raises Chaos: more rats, weepers and guards appear, characters react, and the final mission and ending turn darker.
One ending: the Citadel finale plays out the same for every player, regardless of how each chapter was fought.

sources.note: Dishonored: the world reacts to how you play, outcomes change with your approach
Half-Life 2: single campaign continuing into the episodes

options.how: Five main endings, A to E, arrive over successive playthroughs; 20 minor endings fire mostly when you fail or abandon objectives.
Every player heads for the same looming mountaintop; companions met on the way change the feel of the trip, not where it ends.

sources.note: NieR:Automata: five primary endings A to E plus 20 minor endings from failed objectives
Journey: the looming mountaintop is your goal, with companions along the way

options.how: Rewind time to change events; choices made across five episodes lead to multiple endings.
A fixed chapter sequence builds to the same final confrontation for everyone; puzzles have set solutions and the plot does not branch.

sources.note: Life is Strange: rewind time, multiple endings depending on the choices you make
Portal 2: single-player story campaign through Aperture test chambers
Portal 2: campaign structure and the game's final ending in Wheatley's facility

options.how: Thousands of choices feed dozens of possible endings; characters can die and the story continues, so each run concludes differently.
Every player opens the Vault and reaches the same G-Man finale that rewrites Eli's fate; no earlier choice changes how it ends.

sources.note: Detroit: Become Human: thousands of choices and dozens of possible endings; the story continues if a character dies
Half-Life: Alyx: storyline ending at the Vault with the G-Man and Eli; no choice alters it
